item.title: How to Create Executable JAR Files in Java
item.description:
“How to Create Executable JAR Files in Java”

A JAR (Java Archive) file is essentially a package containing multiple Java class files, associated metadata, and resources. Making a JAR file executable allows it to be run directly as a standalone application. This is typically achieved by specifying a main class, which is the entry point for your Java program.

Here are several approaches to create executable JAR files:

Solution 1: Using the jar Command with a Manifest File

To make a JAR file executable, you need to declare the main class within a Manifest file.

item.title: Modifying Files Inside a Running Java JAR Archive Strategies and Pitfalls
item.description:
“Modifying Files Inside a Running Java JAR Archive Strategies and Pitfalls”

A common requirement in application development involves persisting or altering configuration files that are initially bundled inside a deployed Java Archive (.jar). When an application attempts to write changes directly back into its own running JAR file, significant technical hurdles and platform limitations often arise. What are the established patterns and alternatives for handling data that needs to survive application restarts, given the inherent read-only nature of resources loaded from an executing JAR?

item.title: Java JAR Executable Error: 'no main manifest attribute'
item.description:
“Java JAR Executable Error: ’no main manifest attribute'”

Encountering the dreaded "no main manifest attribute, or bundle symbol namespace contains invalid" error when trying to execute a Java JAR file can be a significant roadblock. This message typically indicates that the Java Virtual Machine (JVM) cannot locate the entry point to your application within the JAR. This usually stems from an improperly constructed executable JAR file, specifically the absence or misconfiguration of the MANIFEST.MF file.
